data.question: Is delivery mode associated with complications?

aiDisclosure.note: Statistics are calculated by deterministic code. The AI selects the method and writes the explanation.
aiDisclosure.dataSent: Question text, column names, inferred types, missing percentages, category labels (up to 15 per column) and aggregate statistics. No row-level values and no columns flagged as personal data.
aiDisclosure.rationale: Testing association between two categorical variables: delivery mode and complication status.

data.interpretation: The chi-square test found a statistically significant association between delivery mode and complications (p = 0.0232, alpha = 0.05), with Cramer's V of 0.207284 indicating a modest effect size. Among 120 deliveries, complications were observed in 9 Caesarean and 7 vaginal cases. This association does not establish causation, and results may be affected by unmeasured confounding and the approximate nature of chi-square p-values for sparse tables.
assumptions: Each observation is assumed to belong to exactly one row and one column category.
limitations: Results use complete cases only. Rows with a missing value in an analysed variable are excluded.
These statistics describe association in this dataset. They do not establish causation.
Unmeasured confounding can affect every association in observational healthcare data.
Chi-square p-values are approximate for sparse tables.
